posts.title: How to Choose Fresh Fish at the Market
posts.excerpt: Clear eyes, red gills, firm flesh: a quick checklist for buying bangus, tilapia and galunggong with confidence.
posts.content:
Fresh fish should smell like the sea, not "fishy". Whether you buy at the palengke or online, these checks help you pick the best of the day's catch.

  • Eyes: clear and bulging, not cloudy or sunken.
  • Gills: bright red or pink, not brown.
  • Flesh: firm and springs back when pressed.
  • Scales: shiny and tightly attached.

Keep it cold

Cook fresh fish within a day, or clean, pat dry and freeze in portions. Our seafood is packed on ice for delivery (demo).

posts.title: A Seasonal Vegetables Guide for Smarter Market Runs
posts.excerpt: Why vegetable prices swing week to week, and how buying in season keeps your budget steady.
posts.content:
Vegetable prices move with weather, harvest cycles and transport. Highland crops like cabbage and carrots often dip after harvest season, while typhoons can push prices up quickly.

  • Watch the price board for items that are trending down.
  • Swap ingredients: pechay for cabbage, sayote for upo.
  • Buy firm vegetables that keep well — carrots, cabbage, onions — when prices are low.

posts.title: Bulk Buying for Carinderias and Sari-Sari Stores
posts.excerpt: How to plan weekly supply, compare price per kilo, and use quotation requests for better rates.
posts.content:
Food businesses buy the same staples every week. Planning ahead lets you negotiate better prices and avoid running out.

  1. List your weekly staples: rice, cooking oil, onions, garlic, eggs, pork.
  2. Compare the price per kilo or litre across pack sizes.
  3. Send a quotation request with your quantity and delivery schedule.
  4. Confirm the quote and set a regular delivery day.

Use Request a Quote for volumes larger than our listed packs.

posts.title: Reading the Price Board: What the Arrows Mean
posts.excerpt: Our price board shows each item's change since its previous price update — here's how to use it.
posts.content:
Every time we update a product's price, the store records it. The arrow next to a price shows the change since the previous update:

  • ▲ green — price went up since the last update.
  • ▼ red — price went down.
  • No arrow — no change recorded yet.

Prices are our store's selling prices, not official government price monitoring. For bulk volumes, request a quotation.

pages.title: Delivery and Returns
pages.content:
Sample policy — review and adapt to your business and to Philippine consumer law (RA 7394) before publishing.

Pickup and delivery

  • Store pickup: choose a pickup point and time at checkout. We email you when the order is packed; bring your order number.
  • Courier delivery (you book): choose a pickup time for your rider, then book Lalamove, Grab Express or any courier to collect from our stall. Courier fees are paid by you directly to the courier.
  • Fresh meat and seafood are packed cold.

Weights and returns

Items sold per kilo are weighed at packing. If an item is short or not fresh on arrival, message us within 24 hours with a photo for a refund or replacement.

pages.title: FAQ
pages.content:
How are per-kilo items priced?

The quantity in your cart is the number of kilos. Natural items vary slightly in weight; any shortfall is refunded.

What do the green and red arrows mean?

They show the change since that item's previous price update in our store.

An item is out of stock. Can you still get it?

Yes — use Request a Quote and we will check supply and get back to you.

Are these real products?

No. This store runs on fictional demo products created to preview the theme.
